instructions: Classify one leaf clause of a spec for a reading view. Choose for you when the clause is user-facing or behavioral (what a user sees or what the result does), or states highly important architecture (a hard-to-reverse boundary, a dependency direction, or a key interface). Choose internals for everything else: implementation detail, mechanics, proofs, fixture or test detail, and minor structure. An acceptance criterion is usually for you; choose internals only when it is about proof or fixture mechanics.

labels.name: for you
labels.description: User-facing or behavioral: what a user sees or what the result does; or highly important architecture: a hard-to-reverse boundary, a dependency direction, or a key interface.

input.clause: The bar sits in page flow, wraps on narrow screens, and never covers the spec or review controls.

When the reviewer pastes a valid commit id, the page re-diffs against it as if picked; an unknown or option-like value shows an inline error and the previous range stays.
